posts.title: 1600: the first step
body: 20 October 2026: the practice account's CC Rating reached 1619. It started at 1500 "(new)" and lost three of its first five games. Since then: 10 sessions, 50 rapid games (15+10, never faster), 27 wins, 7 draws, 16 losses.

The loss to look at: as white against the 1500 in session 2, with 17. Rae1 (Blunder) and 19. Qf3 (Blunder) marked. The review's turning point was 19.Qf3 by Aarav, 25% of the winning chances gone in one move. As in every loss on this road, one move decided it; the review names it, and that move is the lesson.

Openings: the Caro-Kann Defence as Black (answer 1.e4 with ...c6 and ...d5, keep the pawns healthy, and be happy to reach an endgame); the Jobava London as White (d4, Nc3 and Bf4 early, with the knight jumping to b5 to hit c7); the Chebanenko Slav as Black (the Slav with ...a6: hold d5 and get ...b5 in). Each time the same routine from Learn → Openings: the course page, one model game played through, the trainer, and only then the line against a FIDE-rated opponent. From those lines in this stretch: 13 wins, 6 draws, 11 losses.

The rest of Learn, one thing a session: rated puzzles; Guru's strategy lesson; a Guru review of one of my games; an endgame lesson; my last game checked against the 5.4 million games; an endgame from a master's own game; a blindfold puzzle in the Blindfold Gym; a live grandmaster game with the engine on; a new opening in the trainer.
The profile's "How you play" after this stretch: accuracy 95%, opening 93, middlegame 94, endgame 98; sharp moments 98 and calm moves 95. The sharp number is up, which is what the puzzles were for.
5 wins against an opponent one level up (1500, 1400, 1600, 1700, 1700): game two of every session is played a hundred points above the account's own level.
All games so far: 50, 27 wins, 7 draws, 16 losses; 63% won as White and 48% as Black. Next milestone: 1700.

posts.title: From 1500 to 2500: the whole road, in numbers
body: From 19 October 2026 to 20 October 2026: 37 sessions, 173 rapid games, CC Rating 1500 → 2520. 132 wins, 21 draws, 20 losses. This is the whole routine, in order, so that a player can copy it; the full write-up is the case study at /journey/story.

1. Slow games only. Every game was 15+10 against a FIDE-rated opponent at the account's level, and game two of every session against one level up. By opponent: 1400: 6 wins, 0 draws, 4 losses; 1500: 13 wins, 5 draws, 8 losses; 1600: 10 wins, 3 draws, 6 losses; 1700: 14 wins, 0 draws, 0 losses; 1800: 11 wins, 1 draws, 2 losses; 1900: 10 wins, 1 draws, 0 losses; 2000: 10 wins, 0 draws, 0 losses; 2100: 10 wins, 0 draws, 0 losses; 2200: 9 wins, 1 draws, 0 losses; 2300: 10 wins, 1 draws, 0 losses; 2400: 15 wins, 4 draws, 0 losses; 2500: 12 wins, 4 draws, 0 losses; 2600: 2 wins, 1 draws, 0 losses.
2. Review every game, find the one move. Every loss on this road was one move: the review's turning point names it.

3. Learn a line before you play it. The first 9 games from a line seen the same day: 1 wins, 0 draws, 8 losses. Once the course page, a model game and the trainer came first, the next 90: 71 wins, 14 draws, 5 losses.

4. One opening at a time, then many. 26 openings in all: Caro-Kann, Advance Variation, Jobava London, 3...e6, Chebanenko Slav, 5.e3, Sicilian Najdorf, Catalan, Petrov Defence, English Opening, Grünfeld, King's Gambit, Berlin Defence, Jobava London, Sicilian Dragon, Slav Defence, Sicilian Sveshnikov, Pirc Defence, Queen's Indian, Semi-Slav, Modern Benoni, Italian Game, Queen's Gambit, French Defence, Ruy Lopez, Nimzo-Indian, Scotch Game, King's Indian, London System.

5. The rest of Learn, one thing a session: rated puzzles; Guru's strategy lesson; a Guru review of one of my games; an endgame lesson; my last game checked against the 5.4 million games; an endgame from a master's own game; a blindfold puzzle in the Blindfold Gym; a live grandmaster game with the engine on; a new opening in the trainer; my weekly plan; the masters page; the Blindfold Gym; the library; a tactics lesson and a themed puzzle; opening traps and principles; a chapter of a chess book.
6. Read the numbers. The profile at the end: accuracy 97%, opening 98, middlegame 95, endgame 97, sharp moments 97, calm moves undefined. A low number was the next session's work.
The rating is a number. What the routine changed is that, after every game, the next thing to look at is known: one move.
